readerContract.humanQuestion: Why is AI in the climate headlines, and what is the UN actually asking companies to do?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the concrete requests and distinguish political pressure, company promises and measured effects.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No knowledge of UN climate institutions, data-centre infrastructure or energy accounting assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A demand for disclosure can make claims more checkable; a speech is not a new regulation or proof that a particular household bill rose because of AI.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The reader sees AI blamed for power costs and wants to understand what evidence would connect a project to a local consequence.
readerContract.surfaceJob: Daily public-interest brief on September21 UN climate speech, paired with independently reported debate.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can explain the demand and ask a more precise question than whether AI is good or bad for the planet.

canonicalTruth.owner: UNFCCC controls speech wording; AP provides attributed independent context. Neither supplies a local causal bill study.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Check transcript corrections and any resulting policy or company response before publication.

strengthsToUse: Separate the headline rule from its scope
Place each evidence limit beside the claim it limits
End with one action the reader can take

candidateRepairPreflight.authority: UN speech and industry spokesperson both attributed.

draftArchitecture.openingJob: Name the speaker, event date and concrete requests immediately.
causalSequence: AI energy demands are part of the Climate Week public debate.
Stiell asks companies to disclose energy/water use and act on targets, efficiency and renewable power.
Disclosed measurements make specific claims more checkable; targets alone describe intentions.
The speech cannot identify causes of one reader’s bill or create a new local rule.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A company promising to become greener has stated an intention; a dated record of a named facility’s electricity and water use gives something specific to inspect. Hypothetical, not a claim about one company.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: When a headline says the UN puts AI companies on notice, distinguish criticism and requests from a binding order.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: For a local project ask which site, reporting period, energy/water measurements and decision are being discussed.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; The Cocktail Party Explanation; Class Notes; Sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Public-interest relevance does not require a workplace task. No invented personal savings or dramatic per-prompt number.

humourPlan.noneReason: A precise account of the demand is more useful than a decorative environmental joke.

readerQuestions.question: What exactly is he asking AI companies to do?
Does this establish why my energy bill changed?
Did a new rule take effect?

draftArchitecture.presentationPlan: Story-specific art still required before editorial call; no borrowed MAiVEN/TRAiLBLAZER image or generic AI newspaper.
draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: The UN climate chief wants measurable company action and information; his speech does not itself change a household bill or impose a rule.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Brief direct report: named requests, concrete difference between a promise and a reported measurement, then the limits of what a speech establishes.
